parts.name: Root
parts.description: The container with the state. It holds the search text, the local filter, and the virtual focus. It also sets the ARIA relation between the input and the list.

props.name: id
props.description: A stable id, from which the component makes its internal ARIA ids. Give one on a server.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Stops all of the user interaction.

props.name: readonly
props.description: Keeps the input focusable, but stops the changes of the search text and of the selection.

props.name: inputValue
props.description: The search text. You can bind it with `bind:inputValue`.

props.name: defaultInputValue
props.description: The search text at the start, for when the component controls the state.

props.name: filter
props.description:
The local filter function. The default compares the text and ignores the letter case. Set it
to `null` to stop the local filter, for example when a server sends the filtered results.

props.name: autoHighlight
props.description: Highlights the first item that agrees with the search text, each time that text changes.

props.name: onInputChange
props.description: The component calls it when the search text changes.

props.name: children
props.description: The autocomplete parts that you assemble.

props.name: class
props.description: The CSS class names of the root element.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The accessible name of the autocomplete group.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The id of the element that gives the autocomplete group its name.

dataAttributes.name: data-disabled
dataAttributes.description: Present when the autocomplete is disabled.

parts.name: Input
parts.description: The search input, with role="searchbox". It keeps the DOM focus while the arrow keys move a virtual focus through the list with aria-activedescendant.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The accessible name of the input.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The id of the element that gives this input its name.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: The id of the element that describes this input, for example the instructions.

props.name: class
props.description: The CSS class names of the input element.

dataAttributes.name: data-disabled
dataAttributes.description: Present when the autocomplete is disabled.

dataAttributes.name: data-focus-visible
dataAttributes.description: Present while the focus must be visible (keyboard modality).

dataAttributes.name: data-focused
dataAttributes.description: Present while the input has focus.

dataAttributes.name: data-readonly
dataAttributes.description: Present when the autocomplete is readonly.

parts.name: List
parts.description: The listbox of filtered options, which the user always sees. It accepts the same selection props as ListBox.Root: selectionMode, value, defaultValue, and onChange.

props.name: items
props.description: The items, for a list that the component makes from an array.

props.name: children
props.description: The content of the list. From an array of items, it receives one item.

props.name: selectionBehavior
props.description:
The behavior of the selection: 'toggle' lets the user remove a selection, and 'replace' always
selects.

props.name: getItemKey
props.description:
Reads the key of an item. This is the same value as the `id` of `ListBox.Item`.

You need it only with `virtualizer`. Without it, a Shift range is measured over the options in
the DOM. In a virtualized list, those are only the rows near the viewport, thus the range
stops at the scroll position of the user.

props.name: disabledKeys
props.description: The keys of the items that must be disabled. The user cannot select them.

props.name: selectionMode
props.description: The selection mode: 'single' permits one selection, and 'multiple' permits more than one.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected keys. By default it goes in the two directions: use `bind:value`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The selection at the start, for when you give no `value`.

props.name: controlledValue
props.description:
Give your own code full control of the selection. The component stops to write back to
`value`, and it reports only through `onChange`. Thus the parent can refuse a change: the
parent does not send the new selection down. The default is off, because `bind:value` is the
usual case and it needs the write-back.

props.name: header
props.description:
The rows in the listbox above the items, for example an action row such as "Create …". They
are not in `children`, because from an array of items the component calls that snippet one
time for each item.

In a virtualized list, the keyboard does not go into these rows. There, the keys move through
the array of the items, and these rows are not in it.

props.name: class
props.description: The CSS class names of the listbox container.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The accessible name of the listbox. A screen reader announces it.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description:
The id of an element that the user sees, and that gives the listbox its name. Use it in place
of `aria-label` when the list already has a heading.

props.name: onChange
props.description: The component calls it when the selection changes.

props.name: loop
props.description:
At the last item, the arrow keys move the focus to the first item, and at the first item, to
the last one.

props.name: typeahead
props.description: When the user types a character, the focus moves to the option whose text agrees with it.

props.name: virtualizer
props.description:
Makes only the rows near the viewport, and not all of the rows.

The component obeys it only with `items`. The listbox must control the loop to cut it, thus a
list written as static children is never virtualized.

All of the rows must have the same height. This is what lets the component calculate the
scrollbar without a measurement of each row. The component measures the height from the first
row, but `rowHeight` replaces that measurement. Thus a list with your own styles needs no
fixed number.

The listbox element is the element that scrolls. Give it a maximum height and `overflow-y:
auto`. A long list without a virtualizer needs the same.

parts.name: Item
parts.description: An option in the list that the user can select. The filter compares its textValue with the search text. It shows its selection state and its focus state in data attributes.

props.name: id
props.description: The unique identifier of this item. The component uses it for the selection.

props.name: textValue
props.description: The text for the typeahead. If you give none, the component reads it from the content.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables this item. The user cannot select it.

props.name: class
props.description: The CSS class names of the item element.

props.name: children
props.description: The content of the item.

props.name: pressed
props.description: Replaces the pressed state. With this prop, the component uses your value and not its own.

parts.name: ItemIndicator
parts.description: The mark in an item while the item is selected. The default is a check mark icon.

props.name: children
props.description: The content while the item is selected. The default is a check mark icon.

props.name: forceMount
props.description: Keeps the indicator in the DOM, for each selection state.

props.name: class
props.description: The CSS class names of the indicator element.

dataAttributes.name: data-state
dataAttributes.description: "checked" while the item is selected, "unchecked" otherwise.

parts.name: Empty
parts.description: What the list shows when no option agrees with the search text.

props.name: children
props.description: The content while the list is empty. The default is "No results".

props.name: class
props.description: The CSS class names of the empty-state element.

parts.name: Status
parts.description: A hidden aria-live="polite" region. It announces the number of the results to a screen reader.

props.name: formatMessage
props.default:
(count: number) =>
			count === 0 ? 'No results available' : `${count} result${count === 1 ? '' : 's'} available`
props.description: Makes the announced message from the number of the items that the user sees.
